events.title: ENIAC formally dedicated
events.summary: ENIAC was formally dedicated at the University of Pennsylvania on February 15, 1946 — a pioneering large-scale electronic digital computer announced to the public the night before.
events.about: ENIAC filled a room with 17,000 vacuum tubes and computed artillery trajectories thousands of times faster than human calculators. Programmers rewired panels and set switches to change programs — no stored program yet, but it proved electronic computation at scale was possible. The War Department had announced the machine on February 14; the dedication dinner and demonstration followed on February 15.

narrative.whyChosen: ENIAC was among the first large-scale electronic computers to operate as a reprogrammable digital machine.
narrative.whyImportant: It demonstrated that computation could be automated electronically — a foundation for later stored-program designs.
narrative.problemSolved: World War II ballistics tables took weeks of human calculation; the Army needed faster, repeatable numerical work.
